newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED CRUSH LEEDS DESPITE CANTONA MISS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED CRUSH LEEDS DESPITE CANTONA MISS.

text.p: Eric Cantona missed a first-half penalty against his old club Leeds, but his Manchester United side still cruised to a 4-0 away win on Saturday to put their English title defence back on track.

Cantona, who walked out on the Yorkshire side in 1992 within months of helping them to the championship, sent goalkeeper Nigel Martyn the wrong way from the spot kick but rolled the ball wide of the post.
But the Frenchman, captain this season, made amends by scoring United's fourth goal in the final minute.
Earlier, a bizarre own-goal from Martyn, and strikes from Nicky Butt and Czech international Karel Poborsky, set the defending champions on their way.
There were also 4-0 wins for Wimbledon and Middlesbrough, for whom Fabrizio Ravanelli scored his fifth and sixth goals of the season.
But no-one overhauled Sheffield Wednesday at the top of the league, even though they lost 2-0 at home to Chelsea. It was their first defeat of the season.
Wednesday have 12 points from five games, with Chelsea one point behind in second place.
Wednesday's defeat terminated the last 100 percent record in the premier league and left Liverpool, Manchester United and Chelsea as the unbeaten sides.
Liverpool moved third after spoiling Southampton manager Graeme Souness's return to Anfield with a 2-1 win, courtesy of an 89th-minute winner from Steve McManaman.

Stan Collymore, rumoured to be on his way out of Anfield, scored his first goal of the season to give his side the lead, but former Liverpool reserve team player Jim Magilton equalised on 58 minutes with Southampton's first real attack.
The match looked to be heading for a frustrating draw for Liverpool until McManaman took advantage of an awful back-pass from substitute Neil Heaney to score.

Newcastle triumphed by the same 2-1 scoreline at Tottenham thanks to two goals from England striker Les Ferdinand, determined to prove he is more than just a sidekick for 15 million pounds ($23.5 million) signing Alan Shearer.
Spurs took the lead through 18-year-old Rory Allen, making an emergency debut for the injury-hit Londoners.
But Ferdinand hit back before halftime, pouncing on a loose ball after a shot from Shearer was parried by reserve England goalkeeper Ian Walker.

Just after the hour, Ferdinand scored his second winner of the week -- adding to his deciding strike against neighbours Sunderland on Wednesday -- to lift Kevin Keegan's side into sixth place with nine points from five games.
Arsenal showed typical fighting spirit at Villa Park, fighting back from 2-0 down for the second time in a week to earn a point in a thrilling match between two of England's UEFA Cup hopefuls.
Yugoslav Savo Milosovic scored twice for Villa, who appeared to be on course for their fourth consecutive league win.
But Paul Merson gave Arsenal hope with a 70th minute strike, and defender Andy Linighan headed home from a corner deep into injury time to ensure the Londoners left with a point.

It was the second time this week that Arsenal, still waiting to hear when Frenchman Arsene Wenger will join them as manager, had overcome a 2-0 deficit to earn a point. On Wednesday, they shared in a six-goal thriller with Chelsea at Highbury.
Arsenal are now eighth, level on points with Middlesbrough, who followed up their 4-1 midweek win against West Ham with a 4-0 demolition of bottom club Coventry.
Ravanelli put them ahead from a corner after just three minutes, and Brazilian Juninho doubled the tall before halftime lead with a sweetly timed left-foot drive.
The second half was a repeat of the first, with both players adding a goal apiece.
